rendered: Short answer: the documents do not describe lithium-free cathodes. The cathodes they discuss are still lithium-based. What they cover is cobalt-free cathodes, for example the NFA class, which is described as a novel class of nickel rich, cobalt-free Li-ion cathodes: [1]. The sodium papers are the closest thing to a lithium-free route. The first is a room-temperature sodium sulfur battery built from [2], all described as cheap and earth abundant. The second is an anode-free sodium battery whose full cell uses a pre-sodiated pyrite cathode: [3]. Sodium is 1000[4] times more abundant than lithium, but sodium-ion batteries have traded this for energy density: [5]. So sodium chemistries can sidestep lithium, but none of these papers reports a lithium-free cathode in the Li-ion sense. The cathode work in the other papers is about cobalt, not lithium.
